practices.practice: Create and reuse a single MongoClient per process (singleton) rather than creating a new client per request; initialize it once and reuse across handlers.
practices.prior_belief: Use a single MongoClient (driver) instance per process and reuse it across requests (do not create a new client per HTTP request); set sensible timeouts such as serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5000 and socketTimeoutMS=300000 when constructing the client.

practices.practice: Keep the cluster connection string/credentials out of source control by reading the connection URI from environment variables (e.g. DOCUMENTDB_URI) or a secret store and providing only a placeholder in .env.example.
practices.prior_belief: Keep the cluster connection string/credential out of source control: read it from an environment variable (e.g. DOCUMENTDB_URI) or from Azure Key Vault at runtime; never write the real URI/value into files, logs or repo artifacts (.env.example should contain a placeholder).

practices.practice: Require TLS for all client connections to Azure DocumentDB and do not disable certificate validation in production; install CA bundles in restricted environments instead of bypassing TLS verification.
practices.prior_belief: Require TLS for all client connections (e.g. tls=true / tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false in the URI or equivalent driver options) and verify server certificates to avoid MITM attacks.

practices.practice: Enable driver retryable operations (e.g. retryWrites/retryReads) and implement application-level idempotency (idempotency keys or unique constraints) when you need to safely retry operations.
practices.prior_belief: Enable retryable writes (retryWrites=true) and implement idempotency keys for operations that must not be duplicated (or deduplicate on unique keys) to safely retry transient failures.

practices.practice: Choose explicit readPreference and writeConcern tuned to your correctness and latency needs (e.g., prefer primary reads for freshest data; use appropriate write concern for durability), and document these settings in the client configuration.
practices.prior_belief: Choose an explicit readPreference and writeConcern appropriate to correctness/latency: use primary (or primaryPreferred) reads for freshest data and w=majority for durable writes where correctness matters; document and assert these in the client configuration.
practices.how_found: searches: "Azure DocumentDB writeConcern w=majority", "Azure DocumentDB readPreference guidance", "Azure DocumentDB writeConcern documentation"

practices.practice: Create a compound index following ESR (Equality → Sort → Range), for example a compound index on { strategy_id: 1, timestamp: -1 } to serve time-range and sorted queries per strategy.
practices.prior_belief: Create a compound ascending index on { strategy_id: 1, timestamp: 1 } to support efficient time-range queries and aggregations per strategy; ensure the index exists before running aggregation-heavy workloads.

practices.practice: Add additional indexes for common filters and query shapes (equality fields first) and prefer a well-designed compound index over many single-field indexes; review index budget and drop unused indexes.
practices.prior_belief: Add additional indexes for common filters: e.g. { strategy_id:1, event_type:1, timestamp:1 } or single-field indexes on event_type and strategy_id so match stages are covered and index intersection can be used.

practices.practice: When storing vectors for similarity search, store normalized float vectors and create an appropriate vector index (choose DiskANN, HNSW or IVF per scale), store model/dimensions metadata, and tune index parameters (e.g., lBuild, lSearch, maxDegree) for recall/latency tradeoffs.
practices.prior_belief: If storing vectors for vector search, store them in a dedicated field as a flat float32 array (normalized if using cosine) and create a vector index with the cluster-supported algorithm (e.g. HNSW with parameters m and efConstruction) on that field; keep vectors immutable on write.

practices.practice: Model events as immutable append-only documents with fields like type, strategy_id, timestamp and pnl and use deterministic IDs or monotonic sequence fields to preserve ordering and prevent accidental mutation.
practices.prior_belief: Model events as immutable documents with at minimum: type (signal/execution/outcome), strategy_id, ISO-8601 timestamp, pnl (signed numeric), and a deterministic id (UUID or composite of strategy_id+timestamp); include a monotonic trade_seq or insertion timestamp to guarantee ordering.
practices.how_found: searches: "Azure DocumentDB immutable events best practices", "Azure DocumentDB append-only event modeling", "DocumentDB event sourcing patterns"

practices.practice: Prefer single-document updates and inserts; use multi-document transactions only when absolutely required because of their performance cost and complexity, and monitor their impact if used.
practices.prior_belief: Prefer single-document updates/inserts to avoid multi-document transactions; when multi-document atomicity is required, use MongoDB transactions sparingly and monitor their performance impact.
practices.how_found: searches: "Azure DocumentDB multi-document transactions performance", "DocumentDB transactions guidance"

practices.practice: Compute aggregates like win rate, average and total P&L using server-side aggregation pipelines ($match → $group → $project) and retrieve ordered series for cumulative/drawdown calculations; for very large aggregations consider allowDiskUse for server-side sorts or spilling.
practices.prior_belief: Compute win rate, average P&L, and total P&L using MongoDB aggregation pipelines (e.g. $match by strategy_id and date range, $group to compute counts/sums/avg); set allowDiskUse: true for aggregations that could exceed RAM.
practices.how_found: searches: "Azure DocumentDB aggregation allowDiskUse", "Azure DocumentDB aggregation pipelines best practices", "DocumentDB aggregation allowDiskUse"

practices.practice: For server-side cumulative metrics and drawdown, prefer $setWindowFields if the cluster supports it; if not available compute cumulative series client-side after retrieving an ordered series from the DB.
practices.prior_belief: For server-side cumulative or drawdown computations, prefer $setWindowFields (window functions) if available in the cluster version; if not, compute deterministic max-drawdown client-side from time-ordered cumulative P&L series.
practices.how_found: searches: "Azure DocumentDB $setWindowFields support", "DocumentDB window functions setWindowFields"

practices.practice: Order aggregation pipeline stages to reduce work early: apply $match and $project early (to shrink documents) before $group, and place $sort after a selective $match and before windowing when possible so indexes can be used.
practices.prior_belief: When aggregating many documents, pipeline stage order matters: early $match and $project to reduce document size before $group or $sort; place $sort after $match and before windowing operations when possible to leverage indexes.

practices.practice: Use range-based (cursor) pagination keyed on timestamp or a monotonic trade sequence rather than skip/limit for large collections to avoid high scan costs and poor performance.
practices.prior_belief: Use range-based (timestamp or trade_seq) pagination instead of skip/limit for large collections to avoid high-scanning costs; use the compound strategy_id+timestamp index to do efficient range scans per strategy.
practices.how_found: searches: "Azure DocumentDB pagination skip limit vs range", "DocumentDB skip limit performance guidance"

practices.practice: Call explain('executionStats') on representative queries and aggregations in development to verify index usage (IXSCAN vs COLLSCAN) and to check keysExamined/docsExamined ratios.
practices.prior_belief: Always call explain() on representative queries/aggregations in dev to verify index usage and adjust indexes or pipeline stage order if the query plan indicates collection scans or high memory use.

practices.practice: Implement exponential backoff with jitter for client-side retries (initial delay ~100–200ms, exponential factor ~2, max attempts 3–5) and treat some server error codes (rate-limit, etc.) specially as retryable or non-retryable.
practices.prior_belief: Implement client-side exponential backoff and jitter for retrying transient network errors (e.g. with an initial delay ~100–200ms, exponential factor 2, max attempts 3–5) and treat some server error codes as non-retryable.

practices.practice: Use a TTL index for ephemeral or debug events instead of manual deletes: createIndex({ expiresAt: 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: 0 }) or similar, remembering TTL requires a Date field and background sweeper granularity (~60s).
practices.prior_belief: Add a TTL index for ephemeral or debug events (createIndex({ created_at: 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: N })) rather than deleting them manually when you want automatic expiration.

practices.practice: Enforce collection-level validation (JSON Schema) to require and type-check fields such as strategy_id, event_type, timestamp and pnl to prevent invalid events from being stored.
practices.prior_belief: Enforce a collection-level schema validator (JSON Schema) to ensure required fields like strategy_id, event_type, timestamp and pnl are present and of the correct type to prevent corrupt/invalid events from being stored.
practices.how_found: searches: "Azure DocumentDB schema validation json schema", "DocumentDB collection validator JSON Schema"

practices.practice: Monitor cluster metrics (CPU, memory, IOPS, connections) and set alerts; scale compute or I/O proactively (choose appropriate node size or enable autoscaling) to handle ingestion spikes and avoid throttling.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor cluster resource usage and scale compute or I/O proactively: for a managed Azure DocumentDB cluster pick higher node size (e.g. M-series) or enable autoscaling to absorb ingestion spikes and avoid RU throttling.

practices.practice: Rely on the service's automatic backups (documented retention) and also export/validate backups periodically; use test restores to ensure recoverability.
practices.prior_belief: Regularly back up or export critical trading data and the indexes (scheduled snapshots or periodic mongodump/mongoexport) and validate backups by doing test restores.

practices.practice: Sanitize and redact sensitive data before sending any application data to an LLM; include only the fields required for the prompt and never embed connection strings, secrets or PII.
practices.prior_belief: Sanitize and redact sensitive information before sending aggregated stats or event data to an LLM and include only the fields needed in the LLM prompt (avoid embedding raw connection strings, API keys, or PII in prompts).
practices.how_found: searches: "Azure DocumentDB LLM prompt data redaction", "best practices LLM prompt sanitize PII"

practices.practice: Instrument and export metrics for operation latency, error counts, index usage and document growth and integrate these with Azure Monitor or Log Analytics to detect slow aggregations and index issues.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and emit metrics for operation latency, error counts, index usage and document growth; integrate with Azure Monitor or your APM so you can detect slow aggregations and unindexed filters quickly.

practices.practice: Design seed scripts and tests to be idempotent: guard with existence checks or deterministic IDs so repeated runs do not create duplicate documents.
practices.prior_belief: Design the seeding and tests to be idempotent: test fixtures should insert documents with deterministic IDs or delete the created documents at teardown so repeated runs against the same database do not accumulate duplicates.

practices.practice: When combining vector similarity with predicate filters, apply selective predicate filters first to reduce the candidate set, or use the DB's integrated vector+filter search if supported.
practices.prior_belief: When combining vector similarity with predicate filters, perform the filter ($match) first (if selective) to reduce candidate set, then run vector search on the reduced set or use the DB’s integrated vector + filter search capability if available.

practices.practice: Use Azure DocumentDB's full-text search pipeline: createSearchIndexes to define FTS indexes and query them with the $search aggregation stage (prefer this over community $text).
Enable network isolation (Private Endpoint / firewall rules) and prefer Microsoft Entra ID + RBAC and customer-managed keys (CMK) for production security posture and least-privilege access.

For production vector indexes choose an index type by scale (prefer DiskANN for large collections, HNSW for moderate scale, IVF for small) and tune lBuild/lSearch/maxDegree to trade build time, memory and recall.
